memory_candidates.content: In bash, a function definition nested inside another function body is only registered when execution reaches that statement. A large script whose entire body from an early line through EOF lives inside one main() invoked on the last line (the shape of agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh) therefore has a strict definition-before-use ordering constraint INSIDE that body: calling a helper defined further down returns 127 ('command not found'), and under `set -euo pipefail` an `if helper ...; then` guard silently swallows that 127 as a false branch. The predicate compiles, shellcheck stays clean, and the rule never fires. When planning a new call site in such a script, verify the callee's definition line is strictly less than the call line, and hoist the definition rather than trusting top-of-file-style ordering intuition.
